newsitem.title: USA: NYS Democrats to try to expand rent controls-paper.
newsitem.headline: NYS Democrats to try to expand rent controls-paper.

text.p: The Democrat-controlled New York State Assembly on Thursday plans to propose expanded rent control rules, countering the Republican-led Senate, whose leader wants deregulation, Daily News reported Thursday.
The paper said that while the plan has no chance of approval as it stands, it stakes out a starting point for negotiations between the two houses, which are led by different political parties.

There has been widespread speculation that the Senate's proposal to deregulate the market, which mainly affects New York City residents, would be used as political leverage against the Assembly Speaker, Sheldon Silver (D-Manhattan).
Specifically, the paper said the Democrat proposal would:
--Make state rent protections permanent, eliminating battles over renewing such laws.
--Eliminate apartment leases, entitling tenants to permanent occupancy with periodic rent hikes decided by the city Rent Guidelines Board.
--Set a 5.0 percent cap on the maximum rent increase allowed when rent-regulated apartments become vacant, down from the 9 percent allowed now.

--Limit rent increases allowed for major improvements, like window replacemtns. Landlords would be allowed to charge a maximum of 6 percent rent surcharge for the work, and it would expire once the improvements were paid for. Current law authorizes a permanent 6 percent hike.
The bill's chief sponsor is Assembly Housing Committee Chairman Vito Lpez (D-Brooklyn), who at 1100 EST is expected to announce the proposal at a news conference.
